target: Förutsatt att vädret tillåter åker vi.
english: Provided the weather permits, we'll go.
tip: "Förutsatt att" = provided that / assuming that.

target: Vi äter surströmming en gång om året.
english: We eat surströmming once a year.
tip: Surströmming (fermented herring) is notoriously smelly – eaten outdoors in late summer.

target: Även om det var dyrt köpte vi det.
english: Even though it was expensive we bought it.
tip: "Även om" = even if/though. Triggers subordinate word order in the if-clause.

target: Ha en bra dag!
english: Have a nice day!
tip: "Att" + past tense in exclamations expresses appreciation for completed actions.

target: Var snäll och sitt ner.
english: Please sit down.
tip: 'Var snäll och...' (Be kind and...) is a polite way to make requests in Swedish.

target: Kör försiktigt, det är halt.
english: Drive carefully, it's slippery.
tip: "Halt" = slippery (ice). "Kör försiktigt" = drive carefully (imperative).

target: Jag är glad att träffa dig.
english: I am happy to meet you.
tip: "Glad" + "att" + infinitive: happy to do something.

target: Gå till Skansen sedan länge idag!
english: Go to Skansen for a long time today!
tip: Skansen is the world's first open-air museum, located in Stockholm.

target: Det var som om tiden stod stilla.
english: It was as if time stood still.
tip: "Som om" = as if. Creates hypothetical comparison.

target: Jag tror att det kommer att gå bra.
english: I think it will go well.
tip: "Att" clauses use BISATS word order: subject + inte/aldrig + verb.

target: Det var precis som om tiden hade stått helt stilla.
english: It was exactly as if time had stood completely still.
tip: "Som om" = as if. Takes subordinate clause word order.

target: Även om vägen är lång kommer vi dit till slut.
english: Even if the road is long, we will get there eventually.
tip: "Även om" = even if/though. Introduces a concessive clause.

target: Oavsett utfall är jag nöjd.
english: Regardless of the outcome, I'm satisfied.
tip: "Oavsett" = regardless of. Takes noun or subordinate clause.

target: Om det regnar stannar vi inne.
english: If it rains we'll stay inside.
tip: "Om" = if (conditional). The subordinate clause often comes first.

target: Trots att det regnade gick vi ut.
english: Although it rained we went out.
tip: "Trots att" = although/despite that.

target: I och med att han slutade fick hon jobbet.
english: Since he quit, she got the job.
tip: "I och med att" = since/given that.

target: Frågeställningen rör sig om huruvida.
english: The research question concerns whether something is the case.
tip: "Huruvida" = whether (formal). Everyday Swedish uses "om" instead.

target: Trots att hon var trött fortsatte hon.
english: Despite being tired she continued.
tip: "Trots att" = despite the fact that. Subclause triggers verb-final order.

target: Det gamla slottet är vackert.
english: The old castle is beautiful.
tip: Double definite: det + gamla + slottet. Three markers of definiteness simultaneously!

target: Vi träffas imorgon på kvällen med vänner.
english: We'll meet tomorrow in the evening with friends.
tip: "Träffas" = meet each other (by arrangement).

target: Hon hittade till slut det förlorade passet i botten av sin väska.
english: She finally found the lost passport in the bottom of her bag.
tip: "Förlorad" = lost (from "förlora"). "Pass" is ett-word: passet. "Förlorade" in definite.

target: Den svenska allemansrätten är unik.
english: The Swedish right to roam is unique.
tip: Allemansrätten allows everyone to walk, camp, and pick berries on any land.

target: Hon frågade om vi hade ätit.
english: She asked if we had eaten.
tip: Swedish marks definiteness with a suffix on the noun itself: 'hund' → 'hunden' (the dog), 'hus' → 'huset' (the house).

target: Lyssna på mig under veckan gärna!
english: Listen to me during the week gladly!
tip: "Lyssna" → imperative "lyssna" (Group 1 keeps -a). "Lyssna på" = listen to.

target: Brevet skickades igår.
english: The letter was sent yesterday.
tip: Past s-passive: skicka → skickades. Add -s to past tense: skickade + s.

target: Vi tar en fika på kafét.
english: We'll have fika at the café.
tip: "Kafé" is ett-word. "Kafét" = the café (definite).

target: Det vita huset är till salu.
english: The white house is for sale.
tip: "Till salu" = for sale. "Vit" → "vita" in definite: den vita, det vita, de vita.

target: De som vill kan följa med snart.
english: Those who want to can come along soon.
tip: "De som" = those who – a very common construction.

target: Jag ska åka till Norge imorgon nu.
english: I'm going to go to Norway tomorrow now.
tip: "Ska" + infinitive expresses plans/intentions. The most common future form.

target: Vi skulle vilja boka ett bord för två.
english: We would like to book a table for two.
tip: "Vi skulle vilja" is the most formal way to make a request.

target: Sjön glittrar i solen.
english: The lake glitters in the sun.
tip: Both "sjön" and "solen" are simple definite – no double definite needed.

target: Maten lagas av kocken.
english: The food is cooked by the chef.
tip: S-passive is more common than bli-passive for habitual/general statements.

target: Den röda stugan ligger vid sjön.
english: The red cottage is by the lake.
tip: Röda stugor (red cottages) are the most iconic image of the Swedish countryside.

target: Boken har översatts till tjugo språk.
english: The book has been translated into twenty languages.
tip: "Har översatts" = has been translated. Perfect s-passive: har + supine + s.

target: Jonglören kastade sex bollar i luften samtidigt.
english: The juggler threw six balls into the air simultaneously.
tip: "Smörgåsbord" is one of few Swedish words used in English.

target: Platsen dit vi reste på kvällen förra året.
english: The place we traveled to in the evening last year.
tip: "Dit" = to where. "Platsen dit" = the place to which.

target: Jag skulle vilja beställa på morgonen förra året.
english: I would like to order in the morning last year.
tip: "Skulle vilja" = would like. The polite standard in restaurants and shops.

target: Dörren öppnas automatiskt.
english: The door opens automatically.
tip: Here "-s" makes it passive: 'the door is opened.' Context tells passive from deponent.

target: Musiken som spelas är fin.
english: The music being played is nice.
tip: "Som spelas" = that is being played. S-passive in relative clause – very natural in Swedish.

target: Allt som allt är jag nöjd.
english: All in all I'm satisfied.
tip: "Allt som allt" = all in all. Very common summary expression.

target: Kvinnan som jobbar på banken är trevlig.
english: The woman who works at the bank is nice.
tip: After "som" as subject, the verb agrees with the antecedent: "kvinnan som jobbar" (she works).

target: Min fru arbetar också på samma kontor som jag.
english: My wife also works at the same office as me.
tip: 'Som' is the universal relative pronoun – it works for who, which, and that: 'mannen som bor här'.

target: Presenterna öppnas på julafton.
english: The presents are opened on Christmas Eve.
tip: In Sweden, presents are opened on Christmas Eve (the 24th), not Christmas Day.

target: Dimman lade sig som ett täcke.
english: The fog settled like a blanket.
tip: Similes with "som" (like/as): "som ett täcke" = like a blanket.

target: Huset ska säljas under sommaren nästa år.
english: The house is going to be sold during the summer next year.
tip: "Ska säljas" = will be sold. Modal + infinitive s-passive. Very common in real estate.

target: Gatan repareras.
english: The street is being repaired.
tip: "Just nu" = right now. S-passive for ongoing actions: "repareras" = is being repaired.

target: Trevligt att träffas.
english: Nice to meet you.
tip: Swedish verbs ending in -s can be passive or deponent (active meaning). Context determines which.

target: Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe.
english: I would like a coffee.
tip: "Skulle vilja" = would like. Very polite way to make requests.

target: En överraskande nyhet väldigt ofta nu.
english: A surprising piece of news very often now.
tip: "Överraskande" (surprising) – present participle (-ande/-ende) never inflects. Same for all forms.

target: Välkommen till Sverige, jag hoppas att du trivs bra här.
english: Welcome to Sweden, I hope you enjoy it here.
tip: 'Hoppas' (to hope) – deponent verb ending in -s but with active meaning.

target: Vi ska ha middag hemma hos oss på fredag kväll.
english: We are having dinner at our place on Friday evening.
tip: 'Ska' + infinitive expresses planned future: 'Jag ska resa imorgon' (I'm going to travel tomorrow).

target: Han har precis blivit klar med att renovera köket och det ser helt annorlunda ut nu.
english: He has just finished renovating the kitchen and it looks completely different now.
tip: "Kokt" = boiled/cooked. Past participle agrees: kokt (ett), kokta (plural/definite).

target: Breven skickades via posten.
english: The letters were sent via mail.
tip: "Via" is used in Swedish just like in English – borrowed from Latin.

target: Vi umgås med grannen hela tiden med vänner.
english: We socialize with the neighbor all the time with friends.
tip: "Umgås" means to socialize or spend time together – an important Swedish concept.

target: De andas tungt efter löpningen ibland till slut.
english: They breathe heavily after the run sometimes in the end.
tip: "Andas" is deponent – always has -s but is active in meaning (to breathe).

target: De brottas på mattan.
english: They wrestle on the mat.
tip: "Brottas" = wrestle. Reciprocal – they wrestle each other.

target: Det teoretiska ramverket baseras på.
english: The theoretical framework is based on.
tip: "Baseras på" = is based on (s-passive). "Ramverk" = framework.

target: Lagen antogs av riksdagen i helgen under sommaren.
english: The law was passed by parliament on the weekend during summer.
tip: "Riksdagen" = the Swedish parliament. "Antog" → "antogs" – just add -s for s-passive past.

target: Alla i Sverige vet att Astrid Lindgren är en levande legend.
english: Everyone in Sweden knows that Astrid Lindgren is a legendary author.
tip: "Levande" = living (present participle). "Leva" → "levande" – a very common form.

target: Vi umgås varje helg.
english: We socialize every weekend.
tip: "Umgås" = spend time together. Very important concept in Swedish social life.
